name: NETWORKING
description: The fundamental architecture and communication protocols enabling data exchange between distributed computing systems.

children.name: LAN
children.description: Local Area Network. A computer network interconnecting computers within a limited area such as a residence, school, or office building, offering high data-transfer rates and low latency.

children.name: Ethernet
children.description: Standard local network technology defining physical and link layer cabling, frame formats, and MAC addressing mechanisms.

children.name: WLAN
children.description: Wireless Local Area Network linking devices through high-frequency radio spectrum according to IEEE 802.11 standards.

children.name: VLAN
children.description: Virtual Local Area Network. A logical subnetwork that groups together collections of network devices across multiple physical switches into isolated broadcast domains, improving security, manageability, and traffic isolation.

children.name: 802.1Q Tagging
children.description: Networking standard supporting VLANs on Ethernet by inserting a 4-byte tag field into frame headers to identify VLAN membership.

children.name: Trunking
children.description: A point-to-point link configured between switches or routers that carries traffic for multiple distinct VLANs simultaneously.

children.name: WAN
children.description: Wide Area Network. Telecommunications network extending across large geographic regions connecting distributed campuses, data centers, and cloud providers.

children.name: SD-WAN
children.description: Software-Defined Wide Area Network managing hybrid connections to route application traffic dynamically based on bandwidth and jitter.

children.name: MPLS
children.description: Multiprotocol Label Switching directing data packets using short path labels rather than complex IP lookup tables.
